newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April domestic vehicle sales fall 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan April domestic vehicle sales fall 12.7 pct.

text.p: Japan's domestic vehicle sales fell 12.7 percent in April from a year earlier to 326,975 units, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said on Thursday.

It was the first decline in eight months on a year-on-year basis and was caused by an increase in Japan's sales tax, which was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1, an association official said.
All Japanese vehicle makers had declines in April except Daihatsu, Suzuki and Fuji Heavy.
All three enjoyed higher sales due to demand for their new recreational vehicles.
Sales by Daihatsu rose 212.7 percent from a year earlier to 4,415, those by Suzuki rose 2.9 percent to 6,020 and Fuji Heavy's rose 35.3 percent to 9,085.
